comparison: Both address cognitive decline findings (C3, C30-C33). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance across multiple cognitive domains, while peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, acknowledging the cognitive findings as having 'substantial impacts' with no specific critiques raised.

Both evaluate polygenic risk score findings (C4, C34-C36). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate methodology despite marginal ADHD significance, while peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the genetic susceptibility results as part of the comprehensive analysis without raising specific concerns.

Both assess the mirroring hypothesis validation (C5, C6, C46-C50, C74). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of formal statistical testing of the mirroring hypothesis, while peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether external validation data should be used and whether previous discoveries support the conclusion.

Both evaluate biological aging associations (C2, C26-C29). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED despite small effect sizes (Cohen's D < 0.1), noting statistical significance and robustness. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about the clinical/biological meaningfulness of the small differences despite statistical significance.

Both address gene expression analysis (C51-C58 for OpenEval; C51-C60 for peer). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate spatial permutation testing, though notes modest variance explained. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the intuitive link between gene expression results and brain structure differences, and asking about overlap with GWAS findings.

Both evaluate GWAS findings (C7, C37, C39, C43 for OpenEval; adds C8, C38 for peer). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate genome-wide significance and adequate sample size. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the genetic results as part of the comprehensive analysis without specific concerns.

Both assess the two-pattern identification (C1, C21-C25, plus C83-C91 for OpenEval). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with comprehensive methodological details and robust evidence from large sample. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the stratification methodology and whether alternative methods like PCA would yield similar results.

Both address longitudinal data limitations (C82). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as an acknowledged limitation with only 11% having follow-up scans. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether external validation data should be used, suggesting concern about the limited longitudinal data and single cohort approach.

OpenEval evaluates gene set enrichment findings (C59-C62) as SUPPORTED with FDR correction, noting reasonable biological interpretation for synaptic and autophagy mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific enrichment claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature contextualization of GWAS findings (C38, C40-C42, C44-C45) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and convergence with prior studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C38 appears in peer R6 context.

OpenEval evaluates the brain aging and bone density genetic overlap inference (C80) as SUPPORTED based on single locus observation, though notes formal genetic correlation would strengthen evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C9-C20) as SUPPORTED, noting they appropriately establish scientific context and rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates Discussion literature citations (C63-C81, C92) as SUPPORTED with appropriate contextualization, though notes C71 clinical applications are speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these Discussion claims.
